title: Degree-one signed shift compatibility of coefficient evaluation
statement: Let H be the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], O the coefficient unit, and M any normalized ringed-site duality model [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. Put T(X)=H(X,O). For every derived object X, the evaluation-transpose bidual map b satisfies b_(X[1]) followed by -(H((sourceShift X 1).hom.op,id_O) followed by (sourceShift (T X) (-1)).inv) = b_X[1]. The source shifts have the complete representative normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. This asserts only the degree-one morphism equality, without exactness, coherent integer shifts, triangle morphisms or slice restriction.

proof.text: Use the fixed coefficientHomResolution I of the coefficient unit. Construct the natural chain map b_E:E to Hom(Hom(E,I),I) by b_E(x)(f)=(-1)^(p*q)f(x). On Hom-product projections, generalHom_d_eval and generalBidualSigns cancel the target differential terms and prove the chain equation. ordinaryBidual_naturality proves naturality on restricted sections. The construction works for an arbitrary I, with no zero-differential hypothesis.

proof.text: For K-flat E take a K-flat quasi-isomorphism a:L to Hom(E,I). Use the two existing normalized uncurry_model equations for a and b_E followed by Hom(a,I), and the symmetry_model equation. bidual_precompose_formula computes the second evaluation as (-1)^(p*q)a(y)(x). totalTensor_generator_ext proves the corresponding total-tensor maps agree from their pure generators. Cancel the tensor comparison and then the isomorphism induced by a to identify Q(b_E), under the fixed doubleComparison, with ringedSiteBidual. Naturality and another K-flat replacement extend this identification to every complex E. This argument uses neither ordinary Hom into the unresolved coefficient nor generic relative-bidual triangle compatibility.

proof.text: Use SignedDoubleHomCone.comparison for the ordinary signed source shifts and its double-Hom comparison chi. The product-projection formula has sign (-1)^(p+t). On b_(E[1]) its combined exponent is p+t+p*(t+1), equal modulo two to (p+1)*t; ordinaryBidual_shift_with and ordinaryBidual_signed_shift therefore prove b_(E[1]) followed by the negative composite of the two signed source shifts equals b_E[1]. unsignedReindex_eval supplies the ordinary reindexing equation.

proof.text: Prove that the inverse ordinary signed source shift satisfies the existing LeftFormula. Strengthen normalized source-shift descent to the fixed resolved coefficient and arbitrary representative isomorphisms; uniqueness of LeftNormalization identifies this descent with sourceShift and proves its source naturality. dualResolutionIso is the fixed coefficientHomResolutionIso inverse, with naturality from the recorded localization factorization. doubleShift_compare transports the ordinary negative double-shift composite through these fixed isomorphisms. The resolved evaluation identification, shift naturality and essential surjectivity of localization give exactly the displayed equality for every derived X.

theorem coefficientBidualEvaluation_shift_one
    (M : RingedSiteDualityModel.{c, v, r, w} J R) (X : D.{c, v, r, w} J R) :
    let O := ringedSiteDualityUnit.{c, v, r, w} J R
    let H := derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R
    let T := Prod.sectL _ O ⋙ H
    ringedSiteBidual M.closed M.symmetric O (X⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
        (-(H.map (Prod.mkHom ((sourceShift.{c, v, r, w} J R X 1).hom.app O).op
          (𝟙 O)) ≫ (sourceShift.{c, v, r, w} J R (T.obj (op X)) (-1)).inv.app O)) =
      (ringedSiteBidual M.closed M.symmetric O X)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧'
